claims.explanation: ABT-751 is a colchicine-site tubulin polymerization inhibitor whose selectivity is likely driven by mitotic/ microtubule dependency and drug efflux/ metabolism rather than a single lineage. Lines with high TUBB/tubulin-pathway expression and intact mitotic checkpoint/apoptosis signaling are expected to be most sensitive, while high ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux or low proliferative/microtubule dependence confers resistance. The observed enrichment of TP53-mutant, highly aneuploid tumor types is consistent with mitotic catastrophe sensitivity, but TP53 alone is not sufficient; co-alterations in PI3K/AKT, BRAF, and cell-cycle genes may further modulate response.

features.basis: ABT-751 binds beta-tubulin at the colchicine site; higher target expression increases drug effect
P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular colchicine-site inhibitor concentration
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with mitotic catastrophe after spindle damage
BRAF-mutant melanomas and other lineages are enriched among sensitive lines
PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation may increase mitotic dependency and drug sensitivity
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines appear among sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, HCC95) are among least affected
CDKN2A loss may release cell-cycle brakes and increase mitotic vulnerability
ATM-mutant lines appear in the least-affected set, possibly reflecting altered checkpoint/apoptosis response
NF1-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via RAS-MAPK-driven proliferation
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear among least affected, suggesting chromatin remodeling affects drug response
KMT2D mutations are frequent in the least-affected lines, suggesting epigenetic resistance
